newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stocks end marginally up led by banks.
newsitem.headline: Athens stocks end marginally up led by banks.

text.p: Greek stocks came off early intraday highs but still managed to close 0.19 percent higher on a strong performance by the banking sector despite a lacklustre performance by stocks in other sectors.
Market participants attributed the outperformance of banks to positive developments for a number of banking heavyweights.

"There are good reasons for rising prices in banking stocks: National heads for a large capital injection, Alpha Credit is completing its rights issue and Commercial will soon be done with loss-making Elefsis shipyards," said Alexis Panagiotopoulos, broker at Intersec.
Current price levels are seen by brokers as a springboard for further gains in 1997 rather than the peak of the recent rally.
"All investors are raising their positions and profit-taking is limited to institutional portfolios which have already reached long-term profit targets," said Panagiotopoulos.
Profit-taking is carried out discretely through block trading which lately constitutes a larger part of daily turnover.
"Retail investors do not relinquish their stocks and institutionals are not exerting pressure on prices," he said.
The rise of the dollar in international markets is viewed favourably for the flow of foreign funds into Greek equities.
"Historically, a stronger dollar has resulted in increased foreign buying which is carried out in blocks," he said.

The Athens general share index settled 0.19 percent or 2.76 points higher on Wednesday, at 1,467.51, from Tuesday's close of 1,464.75. It opened up at 1,466.35 and peaked at 1,472.36 points shortly after.
Banking shares accounted largely for the benchmark index's 0.57 percent rise. Stocks from the leasing and holding sectors also rose. All other sub-indices finished lower.
With a large number of market participants still enjoying an extended Easter vacation, turnover was high at 16.1 billion drachmas on 4.5 million shares traded.

Trading included several blocks in Viohalko, totalling 95,000 shares at around 6,100-6,200 drachmas, Ergobank 10,000 shares at 18,100, Lavipharm 80,000 shares at 2,400 and Avax 104,000 shares at 1,940.
Decliners led advancers 138 to 84 with 20 stocks unchanged on 242 traded.
The Athens bourse will be closed on Thursday in observation of Labour Day. The next trading session will be staged on Friday May 2.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,085.0 - 1,115.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 45 drachmas at 6,245.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $64.26-$65.95. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 2,303-2,501 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $14.12-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
